explanation: The join matches each employee row to the department row with the same department id. That produces one result row per matching employee-department pair, showing each employee with their department name. Because this is an inner join, departments with no employees are excluded.

options.text: Each employee matched with the name of the department they belong to
One row per department, with employee names combined into a single field
Only departments that have no employees
All departments, even if they have no employees, with blank employee names

prompt:
A company stores departments in `Department(dept_id, dept_name)` and employees in `Employee(emp_id, emp_name, dept_id)`, where `Employee.dept_id` references `Department.dept_id`. What does this query return?

```sql
SELECT d.dept_name, e.emp_name
FROM Department d
JOIN Employee e
  ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id
ORDER BY d.dept_name, e.emp_name;
```
